pairs: Occasiones quærit qui vult recedere ab amico:
Whoever has a will to withdraw from a friend, seeks occasions;
omni tempore erit exprobrabilis.
he shall be reproached at all times.
Non recipit stultus verba prudentiæ,
The foolish do not accept words of prudence,
nisi ea dixeris quæ versantur in corde ejus.
unless you say what is already turning in his heart.
Impius,
The impious,
cum in profundum venerit peccatorum,
when he has arrived within the depths of sin,
contemnit;
thinks little of it.
sed sequitur eum ignominia et opprobrium.
But ill repute and disgrace follow him.
Aqua profunda verba ex ore viri,
Words from the mouth of a man are deep waters.
et torrens redundans fons sapientiæ.
And the fountain of wisdom is a torrent overflowing.
Accipere personam impii non est bonum,
It is not good to accept the character of the impious,
ut declines a veritate judicii.
so as to turn away from true judgment.
Labia stulti miscent se rixis,
The lips of the foolish meddle in disputes.
et os ejus jurgia provocat.
And his mouth provokes conflicts.
Os stulti contritio ejus,
The mouth of the foolish is his destruction,
et labia ipsius ruina animæ ejus.
and his own lips are the ruin of his soul.
Verba bilinguis quasi simplicia,
The words of the double-tongued seem simple.
et ipsa perveniunt usque ad interiora ventris.
And they reach even to the interior of the gut.
Pigrum dejicit timor;
Fear casts down the lazy,
animæ autem effeminatorum esurient.
but the souls of the effeminate shall go hungry.
Qui mollis et dissolutus est in opere suo frater est sua opera dissipantis.
Whoever is dissolute and slack in his work is the brother of him who wastes his own works.
Turris fortissima nomen Domini;
The name of the Lord is a very strong tower.
ad ipsum currit justus,
The just one rushes to it,
et exaltabitur.
and he shall be exalted.
Substantia divitis urbs roboris ejus,
The substance of the wealthy is the city of his strength,
et quasi murus validus circumdans eum.
and it is like a strong wall encircling him.
Antequam conteratur, exaltatur cor hominis, et antequam glorificetur, humiliatur.
The heart of a man is exalted before it is crushed and humbled before it is glorified.
Qui prius respondet quam audiat,
Whoever responds before he listens,
stultum se esse demonstrat,
demonstrates himself to be foolish
et confusione dignum.
and deserving of confusion.
Spiritus viri sustentat imbecillitatem suam;
The spirit of a man sustains his weakness.
spiritum vero ad irascendum facilem quis poterit sustinere?
Yet who can sustain a spirit that is easily angered?
Cor prudens possidebit scientiam,
A prudent heart shall possess knowledge.
et auris sapientium quærit doctrinam.
And the ear of the wise seeks doctrine.
Donum hominis dilatat viam ejus,
A man’s gift expands his way
et ante principes spatium ei facit.
and makes space for him before leaders.
Justus prior est accusator sui:
The just is the first accuser of himself;
venit amicus ejus,
his friend arrives
et investigabit eum.
and shall investigate him.
Contradictiones comprimit sors,
Casting a lot suppresses contentions and passes judgment,
et inter potentes quoque dijudicat.
even among the powerful.
Frater qui adjuvatur a fratre quasi civitas firma,
A brother who is helped by a brother is like a reinforced city,
et judicia quasi vectes urbium.
and judgments are like the bars of cities.
De fructu oris viri replebitur venter ejus,
From the fruit of a man’s mouth shall his belly be filled.
et genimina labiorum ipsius saturabunt eum.
And the harvest of his own lips shall satisfy him.
Mors et vita in manu linguæ;
Death and life are in the power of the tongue.
qui diligunt eam comedent fructus ejus.
Whoever values it shall eat from its fruits.
Qui invenit mulierem bonam invenit bonum,
He who has found a good wife has found goodness,
et hauriet jucunditatem a Domino.
and he shall draw contentment from the Lord.
Qui expellit mulierem bonam expellit bonum;
He who expels a good wife expels goodness.
qui autem tenet adulteram stultus est et impius.
But he who holds on to an adulteress is foolish and impious.
Cum obsecrationibus loquetur pauper,
The poor will speak with supplications.
et dives effabitur rigide.
And the rich will express themselves roughly.
Vir amabilis ad societatem magis amicus erit quam frater.
A man amiable to society shall be more friendly than a brother.
